title: Wang et al. 2024 — Brain Treebank: Large-scale intracranial recordings from naturalistic language stimuli
description: The Brain Treebank is a large-scale intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) dataset recorded at 2048 Hz from 10 epilepsy patients while they watched Hollywood movies, totalling about 43 hours across 26 trials. Movie audio was transcribed with manually annotated word onsets, and transcripts were parsed into Universal Dependencies syntax trees, giving time-aligned, language-grounded neural data. This version is converted to BIDS-iEEG (BrainVision) and includes electrode metadata and atlas-derived spatial indices.
methods_description: Intracranial EEG was recorded at 2048 Hz from an average of 168 electrodes per subject (1,688 total) in epilepsy patients undergoing monitoring at Boston Children's Hospital while they passively watched movies. Word onsets in the audio were manually annotated and parsed into Universal Dependencies trees. Per-trial HDF5 files were converted to BIDS-iEEG BrainVision format, with each movie as one run and corrupted electrodes flagged as bad.
